articleTitle: Autonomous control management of synchronous generators in microgrid system
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: Decentralized excitation control based on local asynchronous clock feedback measurement leads to the problem of decentralized incompatibility of excitation controllers, which reduces the ability of excitation control design to improve the stability of power systems. Therefore, the problem of decentralized compatible excitation control is proposed, and the effect of excitation control on the dynamic characteristics of the system under compatible and incompatible modes is compared and analyzed, and the shortcomings of decentralized incompatible excitation control and the advantages of decentralized compatible excitation control are given.

articleTitle: CricketAnalyzer: a smart camera-based system for accurate ball speed detection in cricket
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: Accurate and real-time speed detection of moving objects, such as sports balls, is crucial for sports analytics and performance evaluation. Traditional systems, such as radar guns, are used to detect object speed, but they face issues such as high costs, limited flexibility, and dependency on controlled environments. In this work, we introduce an advanced visual camera-based ball speed detection application, CricketAnalyzer. CricketAnalyzer uses the Yolov11 model for object detection and real-time motion analysis. The CricketAnalyzer identifies the ball and calculates its velocity in various scenarios. The CricketAnalyzer application is deployed on the PakSupercomputing cluster, offering a cost-effective, scalable, and highly accurate solution. It also serves as a potential tool for sports analytics and broader use cases.

articleTitle: Audio-visual information integration for humanoid robot gaze shift
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: A humanoid robot is being designed capable of integrating audio-video signal. To develop a model for sound source localization in humanoid robot. Two USB Sound Card microphones are used for sound acquisition and two cameras are used for object detection. A Raspberry-pi is used as a central unit for image processing and sound source localization. When the video data comes from cameras, it is displayed on the screen in frames, and its image processing is being done in parallel. When the required objects image processing and detection is done, then it came to the tracking process. To track the detected object the centre position is defined and in code the error is defined that the quantity of error is encountered by adjusting the positions of servos. A PWM model had adopted for precise and accurate results. The results shows that when the red object came in front of camera a green rectangle is formed around it and a vertical line a centre, when the object moves the green line moves along the object, due to the movement of green line away from the centre position the servos position is changed to make the green vertical line came to its origin.

articleTitle: Towards enhanced multicasting in software-defined Wi-Fi networks
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: Distributing multimedia content to numerous users via wireless networks is increasingly common. Still, traditional Wi-Fi networks face significant challenges in efficiently managing multitask traffic. These challenges involve limited data throughput for multicast streams and potential interference with other network services. This research includes enhanced multicasting in software-defined Wi-Fi networks (EMSD-Wi-Fi), a centralized approach to multicast management supporting software-defined networking (SDN) fundamentals. Furthermore, we introduce proof-of concept implementation of this methodology, illustrating its versatility and potential across a range of complex scenarios, including enterprise group communications, smart homes, smart health care and campus Wi-Fi networks. Performance evaluation through OMNeT++ demonstrate that the EMSD-Wi-Fi system achieves a 30% enhancement in transmission efficiency compared to conventional multicast schemes. Additionally, it achieved a reduction in channel occupancy times by almost 40% relative to direct multicast service (DMS) and legacy multicast approaches, attributable to optimized channel occupancy and advanced proactive mobility management strategies. This makes EMSD-Wi-Fi highly effective for static and mobile multicast services.

articleTitle: Stacking-based ensemble for cervical cancer detection
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: Cervical cancer remains a critical health challenge, and early detection is essential for effective treatment. This study introduces a robust approach for cervical cancer detection using an ensemble of pre-trained deep learning models DenseNet121, MobileNet, and Xception. Our model is fine-tuned with chosen layers trainable to enhance their performance in classifying cervical cancer images. The ensemble leverages stacking, at which the outputs of the base models are paired into meta-features, and a logistic regression model is used as a metaclassifier to make finalized predictions. Data pre-processing includes normalization augmentation to improve model generalization. A 5-fold cross-validation approach is employed to ensure comprehensive evaluation and robustness. Findings indicate that the stacking-based ensemble attains an overall accuracy of 0.9771, outperforming the individual models in classification accuracy and robustness. The average accuracies of an individual models are as follows: DenseNet121 (0.9491), MobileNet (0.9595), and Xception (0.9086). These findings indicate the effectiveness of integrating multiple deep learning models with stacking for medical image classification.

articleTitle: A decentralized hybrid load-shedding scheme for the prevention of blackouts in power grids
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: In normal conditions, the load and generation of a power system are kept in strict balance to have a constant system frequency. Any variation on the load side is compensated by automatic control loops on the generation side and load management by the System Operator (SO). However, in major system disturbances, the load-generation mismatch is much larger, and the control loops fall short of maintaining the required balance. During this time, if sufficient generation is not injected or the surplus load is not disconnected soon, system frequency drops below the permissible limits, and the whole system collapses resulting in a blackout. To maintain system balance and control system frequency during major disturbance events, the widely used technique to shed excessive load is Under-Frequency Load Shedding (UFLS). The conventional Load Shedding (LS) techniques have several shortcomings i.e. slow operation under-shedding and over-shedding. This paper proposes a Rate of Change of Frequency (ROCOF) driven, decentralized, faster, and reliable LS scheme to disconnect the surplus load of the network in successive stages during major system disturbance events to avoid system blackouts. The performance of the proposed LS scheme was tested on a hardware-based setup and implemented in the National Grid of Pakistan.

articleTitle: Numerical evaluation of heat exchanger using nano-fluids
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: Development in nanotechnology is going up these days. Nanofluids used in engine cooling devices improves the efficiency of the system and helps in increasing the heat transfer rate affectively. Different types of nano-fluids with varying concentrations have been used. Thermophysical properties like dynamic viscosity, thermal conductivity, density and specific heat capacity greatly influences the performance of nanofluids in system. Numerous experimental and numerical studies have been done to evaluate the performance of cooling devices. A numerical evaluation of mini stainless-steel tube (ID=1mm, OD=1.5mm and Effected heated Length=280mm) at steady state condition is performed by using COMSOL Multiphysics 6.2. Mini tube, a heat exchanger is analysed at non-isothermal flow condition. Simulations have been performed by using De-ionized water, and by adding different concentrations of nanoparticles. Boundary conditions applied at the inlet and outlet of the section. Outcomes checked by varying important parameter like Reynolds number. Simulation results compared with experimental analysis which shows that there is energy loss in real testing. Simulated values of heat transfer coefficient and nusselt number are higher than original experiments. Graphical representation of important parameters like heat transfer coefficient and Nusselt number are shown.

articleTitle: Optimising solar energy consumption in grid connected residential photovoltaic (PV) system: a demand side management (DSM) approach for peak production utilisation
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: With the growing electricity demand and tariffs, residential consum ersare opting for rooftop solar systems to susta in their electricity needs. While the houses have a ccess to solar energy during the day, but they still relyheavily on the grid during night, adding stress to national grid and intensifying grid’s energy loss. This paper presents a Dem and Side Management (DSM) strategy designed to optimise solar energy usage in grid connected Photovoltaic (PV) systems within Pakistan residential sector. By implementing DSM strategy, this study encourages consumers to shift their high energy appliances to coincide with peak solar production hours, thus reducing the reliance on the grid during non-solar hours. Solar energy production was assessed using PVsyst software, while energy consumption patterns of households were estimated through data acquisition system and LabVIEW. The DSM technique resulted in more efficient solar energy utilisation, decreased peak demand on the electric system, and less load shedding. This solution promotes the provision of clean energy under the United Nations (UNs) Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) while also a ddressing Pakistan's energy concerns. Finally, the findings support the use of DSM to increase the efficiency of residential PV systems, improve grid stability, and promote green energy culture in Pakistani homes.

articleTitle: Designing efficient cooling systems for lithium battery packs: a particle swarm optimization approach
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: Lithium battery packs must have an efficient cooling and ventilation system to keep electric cars running smoothly and safely. It is becoming increasingly critical to guarantee that the battery packs are uniformly heated. This research aims to provide an optimization design system for automotive packs of lithium batteries to lower the maximum temperature difference (MTD). First, the helical cooling canal and the U-like cooling channel are examined as cooling or heat dissipation architectures. The results show that the cooling performance of the serpentine cooling (SC) channel is better. The design of the helical cooling channel is further enhanced by using an adaptive array of surrogate models that use an improved optimization using the particle swarm’s technique. In comparison to the original design, the improved design reduces MTD by 7.5% and leads to a more consistent distribution of temperatures within a lithium-ion pack, according to the results. Battery pack liquid cooling design may benefit greatly from the insights provided by this optimization methodology.

articleTitle: Heap-based political optimizer
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: A new hybrid metaheuristic algorithm called Heap-Based Political Optimizer (HBPO) has been developed by integrating the ideas from Heap-Based Optimizer (HBO) and Political Optimizer (PO). To tackle the challenging optimization problems, the HBPO mimics corporate hierarchies and political systems observed in the actual world. In contrast to the original PO, HBPO uses a heap-based structure to improve position update methods and population representation, which leads to better exploration and exploitation capabilities. The elimination of party leaders, the incorporation of heap-based relationships, and flexible populations represent some of the primary modifications. 23 benchmark functions used to compare HBPO against PO and HBO. The results demonstrate that HBPO performed better on multimodal and composite functions while maintaining similar performance on unimodal functions. These results showed the robustness and reliability of HBPO in handling high-dimensional optimization problems.

articleTitle: Area-efficient design and UVM based functional verification of APB-UART peripheral
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: The Universal Asynchronous Receiver/Transmitter (UART) is the most common used communication protocol in micro-controllers and applications ranging from embedded systems to telecommunications. The open-source UART code available for research community is Wishbone compatible; however, it has been reported in the technical literature that Advanced Peripheral Bus (APB) protocol is now generally used in modern System on Chips (SoCs). Therefore, to address this gap, in this paper the APB-UART peripheral is first designed and later Universal Verification Methodology (UVM) is used to verify the functional correctness of the proposed design. The designed APB-UART is full duplex, configurable for different baud rate generations, checks for parity and have parametrizable data frame features. The proposed design acheives 100% and 95% functional and code coverage closures. Our designed UVM verification environment is scalable, reusable and the developed soft IP can seamlessly be used in the modern SoCs compatible with APB bus.

articleTitle: State of the art in lifelong learning of robots
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: Learning offers a useful tool for the automatic design of autonomous robots. These Robots show an unprecedented capability to change to a greater extent as they can learn painlessly throughout their life from new tasks and environments. Such an attitude is crucial when deploying independent robots in climates and real-world settings that are dynamic and unpredictable. By learning constantly, the robots are in a position to evolve and improve at every given opportunity. This research outlines shifts in certain pathways at an individual level such as techniques used to prevent drastic memory loss, increasing memory’s fittingness, and usage of two memory systems. Models of human memory and learning as well as specific methods of dual memory structure are utilized to improve the performance of robotic agents and to replicate complex human behaviour. These comparisons allow researchers to get a clear picture of where the field is currently at and also the potential trajectories i t can take. The objective of this paper is to analyse the evolution of various approaches to the task of lifelong learning. It discusses the advantages of lifelong learning of robots and highlights the problems that researchers have faced for this such as catastrophic forgetting, limited scalability, complexity, cost issues, etc., and compares various techniques that have been used to address these problems. This paper discusses the pros and cons of various techniques and provides their comparative analysis.

articleTitle: Experimental evaluation of drying kinetics of biomass powered grain dryer
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: Grain drying is a critical post-harvest process, particularly in developing countries where inadequate drying methods contribute to significant post-harvest losses. Traditional open sun drying is inefficient and weather-dependent, underscoring the need for sustainable and controlled alternatives. This study evaluates the performance of a biomass-powered grain drying system designed to offer smallholder farmers an off-grid, cost-effective solution for reducing moisture content in grains. The dryer's performance was evaluated experimentally using corn grains, focusing on drying kinetics, thermal efficiency, and overall energy performance. The dryer achieved a thermal efficiency of up to 78.09% with a maximum drying rate of 0.118%/min. Experimental results were compared with thin-layer drying models, the Logarithmic model and Page model achieved the best fit. These findings highlight the dryer’s capability to achieve efficient and reliable drying, particularly for grains with high initial moisture content. While the dryer demonstrated acceptable performance, areas for improvement were identified, including thermal losses and airflow distribution, which could be addressed in future versions. The study establishes the biomass-powered dryer as a practical and scalable alternative to conventional drying methods, particularly in resource-constrained environments.

articleTitle: Feasibility of a 10 MW PV system expansion in solar park: energy generation, impact on grid network, and financial perspective
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: Renewable energy systems, primarily solar PV systems, have gained significance worldwide due to the limited accessibility of non-renewable energy sources. This study assesses the operational efficiency and financial feasibility of an additional 10 MW grid-connected PV system at the site, which has an operational 400 MW Solar Park. The primary objective of this study is to design a clean energy system in Pakistan. The designed system operates efficiently, achieving a maximum PR of 83.94% in January, a minimum PR of 74.37% in August, and an annual average PR of 78.19% as well as generating 17,499,000 kWh/year of energy. The designed system demonstrates economic viability with a discounted payback period of 11.5 years and a non-discounted payback period of 3.10 years, and NPV of a PV plant is 576,346 USD. Utilizing software like PVsyst accurate system design as well as effective module layout. The OpenDSS software has been used to simulate the analysis of loss impact on electrical networks with 400 MWp and 410 MWp. From simulation analysis, it is concluded that the addition of 10MW in the existing electrical system is feasible, losses have been reduced due to increased generation and system efficiency. The generated power has been transmitted to the 132 kV GS under both normal and contingency conditions without any transmission constraints.

articleTitle: Design of a dual output voltage, constant current SEPIC-boost converter with PID feedback control
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: In this paper, design of a dual output DC-DC converter based on combination of SEPIC and boost topology is presented. A simple control strategy is achieved by using a single switch to drive both SEPIC and boost circuitry resulting in an economical, simple and practical design. Two different output levels, namely 36 V and 48 V with similar 2 A constant current are successfully generated from a 24 V input supply. Feedback control is applied using Proportional - Integral – Derivative (PID) control where conventional and optimised gain values are integrated in the proposed design. The results show both methods able to produce the desired output levels, but the optimised gain parameters yield better regulation with smaller ripple percentage.

articleTitle: Performance evaluation of TCP congestion control mechanisms for WiGig ad-hoc networks
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: This paper presents an evaluation of six TCP congestion control algorithms i.e. Vegas, Linux Reno, Westwood Plus, YEAH, Cubic, and BBR in WiGig networks operating under the IEEE 802.11ad protocol. Utilizing Network Simulator 3 (NS-3) with the WiGig module, we simulate two distinct network topologies, one with a single flow and another with two competing flows. The algorithms are assessed based on standard network performance metrics, including delay, jitter, and throughput. The study emphasizes the trade-offs associated with each algorithm across various network conditions, highlighting the importance of selecting appropriate congestion control methods suitable for specific application requirements and network environments.

articleTitle: Optimized fractional-order PID controller for temperature control of CSTH: a comparative study with PID cascade controller
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: Controlling the temperature in chemical reactors, heating furnaces, distillation columns, and reboilers for circulating heatin g fluids is crucial across all industries. This project is a simulation-based study where both PID-cascade and fractional order PID (FO-PID) controllers were used to control the temperature of water in the continuously stirred tank heater system. The simulation was designed by using SIMULINK. Initially, the work reproduces results from a previous study that evaluated the performance of PID cascade controller applied for controlling the temperature of continuous stirred tank heater. Building on this foundat ion, a novel fractional-order PID (FO-PID) controller was designed and its parameters were optimized using the Whale Optimizer Algorithm (WOA). Results showed that the FO-PID outperforms the PID-cascade controller in terms of settling time and percentage overshoot. This study demonstrates significant advancements in process innovation and optimization, supporting sustainable industrial systems. The FO-PID controller in comparison to the Cascade PID controller reduced the percentage overshoot by approximately 97%, reduced settling time by 87% and maintained comparable steady-state error.

articleTitle: Stable 2-tert-butyl,1-4 benzoquinone based organic anode for lithium-ion batteries
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) are increasingly acknowledged as up-and-coming contenders for large-scale energy storage applications owing to their superior energy density and exceptional efficiency. However, conventional anode materials' relatively low specific capacity and poor cycling stability hinder their broader adoption in these applications. In this context, organic molecules, with their tunable structures and potential for high-energy storage, present a promising alternative to conventional materials. In this investigation, we report the synthesis and electrochemical characteristics of a nitrogen-enriched organic polymer that integrates benzoquinone and melamine units (BQM). The BQM/g-C3N4 polymer demonstrates exceptional electrochemical properties with high cycling stability. Precisely, the anodic half-cell based on BQM/g-C3N4 delivers a specific capacity of 1100 mAh/g at a current density of 50 mA/g after 200 cycles, highlighting its remarkable cycling stability. This work opens up new avenues for organic polymer-based anode materials and paves the way for further developing advanced and sustainable energy storage systems.

articleTitle: Weed detection and removal using autonomous mobile robot
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: Weed plants are the unwanted plants which grow in crop fields where their growth is not wanted. They consume all the nutrients which are necessary for growth of crop plants. Therefore, their removal is mandatory for proper growth of crop plants. The autonomous weed control robot is used to remove these unwanted weed plants. For removal of weed plants, different traditional methods are being used which damages the crop plants and eventually reduces the yield. Autonomous Weed Control Robot is introduced to control weed plants and to remove them without harming crop plants. This weeds control robot consists of an Ackerman Architecture and delta robot. The delta robot along with two cameras and a technique named visual servoing detects the weed plants and their positions respectively. First of all, through an image acquisition process input image will be acquired from camera and image processing will perform different functions on the input image and provide the position coordinates of weed plants. Then, by using visual servoing technique, delta robot moves to desired location of the weed plants. After that, with the help of a hoe tool the detected weed plants are being removed. Ackerman Architecture will work by navigating itself in the field. The results obtained from this work, is controlled growth rate and removal of weed plants along-with the increase in production of crops yield. Thus, this proposed work will be useful in all the agricultural fields where the usage of modern technology will reduce the use of agrochemicals and herbicides in the fields.

articleTitle: Analysis of decision-making strategies in social networks
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: In the era of social media, platforms have become integral to various domains, particularly business, where trends significantly influence decision-making processes. Despite numerous studies, effective decision-making in social networks remains a challenge. This study addresses these issues by proposing a novel model for analyzing decision-making strategies. A publicly available dataset containing social media user reviews of various products, including attributes such as identification, labels, country, and sentiment, is utilized. The dataset undergoes preprocessing and normalization, incorporating techniques such as tokenization, lemmatization, stop-word removal, and punctuation elimination. Deep learning methodologies are applied for model development and analysis, leveraging Python and the PyCharm framework. The proposed model is rigorously validated using state-of-the-art techniques and evaluated through extensive testing to measure its performance in terms of accuracy. Comparative analysis with recent methods underscores the effectiveness of the model. The findings of this study offer valuable insights for improving decision-making strategies, guiding new product development, and integrating diverse analytical models in social network contexts.

articleTitle: Design, fabrication and analysis of cyclone for the reduction of particulate matter from compression ignition engine
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: In this present era, numerous countries are confronting issues such as air pollution and smog, primarily caused by particulat e matter emitted from engines and car exhausts. This paper offers an extensive examination of the design, fabrication, numerica l simulation, and experimental analysis of a cyclone separator intended to mitigate particulate matter emissions from diesel engines. The emissions that are produced by diesel engines are a significant contributor to the pollution of the air, with particulate matter (PM) being the primary pollutants that are released. The use of cyclone separators, which are well-known for their ease of operation and effectiveness in the removal of particulate matter, is being investigated as a potential miti gation method. The research indicates that cyclone separators are acceptable in terms of both efficiency and cost-effectiveness when it comes to lowering particulate emissions from diesel engines. The most dramatic pressure and velocity reduction in the cyclone were determined to be 993 Pa and 18.6 m/s, respectively. The decrease in temperature has minimal impact on the cyclone's performance. The peak cyclone efficiency for PM10 and PM2.5 was determined to be somewhat below 80% and slightly above 50%, respectively, at maximum velocity. The concentration of PM10 and PM2.5 markedly decreased for the B30 mix in comparison to HSD, but the cyclone also mitigated these emissions to some extent.

articleTitle: Experimental study of the combustion process of vegetable waste oil and diesel mixture in a domestic kitchen for remote regions
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: The main objective of this research study is to evaluate the use of vegetable waste oil as fuel in a domestic kitchen and consists of performing experimental tests using a mixture of domestic vegetable waste oil with commercial diesel. The fuel is a mixture of diesel (100 %, 50 % and 25 %) with vegetable waste oil. This new fuel was tested in a kitchen that uses air to pressurize the fuel. The combustion and water temperatures were measured, and the combustion gases were analyzed. The results indicate that the most suitable mixture for fuel is the ratio of 75 % vegetable waste oil with 25 % diesel, which achieves an efficiency of 45.1%, compared to the efficiency of diesel fuel of 49%. Likewise, the analysis of combustion gases showed a reduction in emissions of CO2 in the mixture compared to diesel, resulting in the mixture of domestic vegetable waste oil being 0.925 % compared to pure diesel which is 1.33 %. In addition, in terms of the emissions analysis, the mixture showed an increase of 9.5 ppm compared to diesel which was 6.5 ppm. Thus, mixing the vegetable waste oil at 75 % proves to be a better alternative in terms of combustion, due to its efficiency, cost, emission of combustion gases and for the re-use of vegetable waste oils available in isolated regions lacking available resources.

articleTitle: Assessment of second-generation biodiesel using computational and experimental methods for the reduction of emissions and promoting environmental sustainability
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: The fast depletion of fossil reserves coupled with uncertainty in petroleum prices and environmental degradation has paved the way for alternative and sustainable energy resources. This study investigates the possibility of using biodiesel as a potential alternative for conventional mineral diesel. Waste cooking oil (WCO) was utilized as a feedstock for biodiesel production where pre-treatment of WCO was done via mineral acids for acid value reduction. Physio-chemical properties including calorific value, density, viscosity, cloud point, and a flashpoint of biodiesel blends were examined according to ASTM standards. Biodiesel blends B10, B20, B30, B40, and B50 were tested using a compression ignition engine. Emissions of carbon monoxide (CO), unburned hydrocarbon (UBHC), and oxides of nitrogen (NOx) were experimentally determined for biodiesel blends and were compared with high-speed diesel (HSD) as a baseline. Experimental results were used to validate various combustion and emissions parameters for diesel and biodiesel. Numerical combustion analysis of biodiesel blends and diesel were performed and compared with experimental results. The combustion temperature was taken from 300 K to 2038 K, 1431 K, 1486 K for B100, diesel, and B50 blends respectively. CFD analyses have obtained the products produced by the combustion of fuels like CO2, H2O, N2, O2, and mass fraction of C17H34O2 in both B100 and diesel. The maximum deviation between experimental and numerical results of diesel and B100 were found to be 5.06% and 5% for NOx, 6% and 5.11% for UBHC, 5.26% and 7.94% for CO.

articleTitle: Multivariate short-term load forecasting based on hybrid deep learning approach
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: Short-term Load Forecasting (STLF) is crucial in planning the safe, reliable and efficient operation of today’s power systems. However, the variability arising from the source load pattern due to increasingly dynamic external influence creates considerable hurdles in precise forecasting. This study introduces an innovative hybrid forecasting model that integrates three state-of-the-art deep learning architectures: Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), and Residual Networks (ResNet) are some of the subtypes of Artificial Neural Networks that have been implemented in deep learning networks. To achieve the goal, the temporal learning ability of LSTM is combined with the feature extraction ability of CNN and the efficient learning ability of ResNet, to capture temporal and spatial features in load data. A preprocessing plan is defined to enhance the quality of data to deal with the anomalies results from the outlier, zero value imputation and normalisation stages. The proposed hybrid model is then analysed and tested with actual load dataset through cross-validation to see performance degradation The proposed hybrid model also cross validated with benchmark standalone LSTM, CNN, ResNet models and traditional machine learning technique. In case of hyperparameters, Bayesian optimization is involved in the last stage to fine tune the results of the model. The analysis shows that the suggested hybrid model yields notably higher levels of prediction accuracy and resilience than all other baseline scenarios. This work demonstrates how proper design of hybrid deep learning architectures can eliminate the difficult of STLF and thus ensure better operation of power systems.

articleTitle: Experimental study of the impact of aluminum foil and Mylar reflectors on solar panel performance
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: This paper aims at investigating the optimization of solar panel performance with the application of reflectors, particularly aluminium foil and Mylar. Each material is highly reflective, and both have been credited with the capability to reflect sunlight to photovoltaic zones. Sensors and an experimental apparatus were incorporated to study the impact of various reflector positioning and configurations as well as the properties of the reflector materials on the efficiency of the solar energy system. The effectiveness was determined under condition testing whereby aluminium foil reflector was discussed tested against the Mylar reflector. Data confirms increases in efficiency of the panel by use of both the materials fluctuations experienced based on orientation of the reflectors. Aluminium foil reflected a better light in some particular directions mor e preferential than Mylar while the latter performed consistently in different orientations. This study therefore calls for effective orientation of the reflector and the choice of the reflector material in order to improve the use of solar energy. The presen t results provide applied implications for increasing the efficiency of photovoltaic systems and optimizing the development of sustainable energy technologies.

articleTitle: Assessment of cross-flow indirect evaporative heat and mass exchanger performance using numerical methods
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: Indirect evaporative air-cooling system is an environmentally sustainable substitute for air-cooling interior spaces especially in hot and dry climates. In this work, a system is numerically simulated which is a heat and mass exchanger comprised of polymeric materials such as polypropylene and non-woven fabric cloth. The numerical simulation is carried out by using COMSOL Multiphysics to pretend the heat and mass exchanger in order to identify the ideal thermal comfort under actual climate conditions. It is noted that the system may higher values of energy efficiency ratio and coefficient of performance, as high as 22.3 and 6.55, respectively. The predicted results demonstrated in the dew-point effectiveness, wet-bulb effectiveness, and cooling capacity where the maximum determined values are 0.6, 0.73, and 471 W, respectively. These predicted findings were validated with experimental results which showed a maximum deviation of around 4.78 %. Based on the numerical simulation study and validation, the indirect evaporative air-cooling system be capable of the designed for different operational conditions and climatic zones as per the requirements of end users.

articleTitle: Hierarchical reinforcement learning for enhancing vehicle-to-grid operations in solar power systems
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: This study proposes a Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning (HRL)-based framework for optimizing Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) operations, with a focus on addressing solar power generation (SPG) forecast errors and facilitating efficient energy exchange between electric vehicles (EVs) and the grid. To tackle the inherent variability of solar energy and dynamic operational scenarios, the proposed approach formulates V2G operations as a multi-level decision-making process. High-level policies are designed to handle global objectives such as grid stability, while low-level policies focus on optimizing battery-level operations. Leveraging simulated SPG data and synthetic forecasts, the HRL framework provides a robust environment for training and evaluation, enabling a detailed exploration of critical parameters like blocking probability thresholds and discount factors. Results show significant reductions in Mean Squared Error (MSE) values and improved SPG forecast accuracy, highlighting the model’s adaptability to dynamic conditions. Training loss trends confirm convergence, and sensitivity analyses underscore the framework’s flexibility under diverse operational scenarios. The findings demonstrate the potential of HRL-based strategies to enhance smart grid efficiency by seamlessly integrating distributed energy resources (DERs), offering a scalable and sustainable solution for modern energy management systems.

articleTitle: Robust sliding modes based distributed control protocol for a class of underactuated nonlinear systems
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: In this paper, finite time sliding mode strategies based distributed control protocol design is presented for a class of uncertain underactuated nonlinear systems. The design process starts by first defining the general nonlinear dynamics of the leader as well as the followers. In the next strep, consensus/synchronization error dynamics are defined which reduce the networked multi-agent system’s dynamics to a single error dynamic system. Then sliding modes based regulating control protocol is designed for the constructed error dynamic system which in turn leads to the synchronization of the networked agents. The overall system’s closed loop stability is rigorously investigated via the Lyapunov stability theory. Finally, a suitable example is considered in the simulation study to comprehensively demonstrate the effectivity of the designed protocol.

articleTitle: Resilience assessment of mobile microgrid scenario for supporting critical infrastructure post-disaster
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: Natural disasters (ND) often disrupt traditional power grids, leaving critical facilities such as hospitals, emergency response centers, and communication hubs vulnerable to extended outages. Mobile microgrids (MMGs) are essential for ensuring the resilience of critical infrastructure during and after disasters. This research explores the resilience assessment of using mobile microgrids to enhance energy resilience for critical infrastructure during and post disasters. It focuses on whether a standardized mobile microgrid, housed within a Truck and weighing limit, can adequately support small critical sites with an average 10 kW load. The analysis assumes scenarios where natural disasters may cause power outages, and existing microgrids are present but lack redundancy to justify the creation of bespoke systems for individual critical loads. To assess the robustness of the suggested mobile microgrid, a system that combines a natural gas generator (NGG), photovoltaic (PV) electricity, and a battery energy storage system (BESS) is designed within the logistical and physical limitations of a typical mobility truck (MT). HOMER Grid software models random outages that can last up to 72 hours and evaluates the architecture using Global Horizontal Irradiance (GHI) data and a randomized 10 kW load profile from Lombok Island, Indonesia. The outcomes demonstrate how the system can supply essential loads using less fossil fuel. According to the results, standardized mobile microgrids provide a practical and quickly deployable alternative for restoring critical infrastructure services in the case of a disaster.

articleTitle: Attention-driven triple path residual 3D CNN for efficient brain tumour detection
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: Brain tumour diagnosis and treatment is a very challenging task as gliomas are most aggressive ones and sometimes lead to fatality. The main focus of this study is to classify the LLG (Low Grade Glioma) and HGG (High Grade Glioma) using MRI (Magnetic Resonance Image). To enhance the feature extraction and preprocessing we introduced a novelty i.e. MHA (Multi Head Attention) which is integrated with a three-path CNN (Convolution Neural Network) design. In each path a distinct multi-scale feature is extracted which are then refined through MHA and embedding concatenation which ensures the precise attention to critical tumour region. This proposed model is the demonstration of how it has superior performance in enhanced distinction of gliomas and overcomes the challenges like diverse image characteristics and subtle tumour boundaries. The Evaluation done on the BraTS dataset shows the improvement and achieved an impressive accuracy of 97.98% and generalizability as compared to the state-of-art models.

articleTitle: Design, optimization and performance analysis of 250 kW permanent magnet machine for hybrid electric propulsion of civil aircrafts
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: Hybrid technology has gained its popularity in recent times. Stringent legislation and environments commitments have increased interest of aviation industry in electrification of aircrafts. Hybrid electric propulsion system is one of the aspects which is being explored to reduce dependence on fuel. The integration of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors (PMSMs) into hybrid electric propulsion systems for civil aircraft represents a significant advancement in aerospace engineering. This study focuses on developing and refining a 250 kW PMSM, engineered to drive ducted fans, an essential element in the propulsion mechanisms of civilian aircraft. The challenge in designing these propulsion systems lies in achieving the optimal balance between high power and torque output and the essential goals of minimizing weight and energy losses. PMSMs emerge as a viable answer to this challenge, due to their remarkable efficiency and compact size. This study seeks to leverage these attributes of PMSMs, to fulfill the requirements of proficient and powerful aircraft propulsion systems. The findings of this study indicates that careful optimization of these dimensions led to reduced hysteresis, eddy current losses and overall weight of the PMSM’s.

articleTitle: Renewable biodiesel production from used cooking oil: pathway towards carbon neutral fuel in alignment with Punjab government policy 2018
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: The production of biodiesel, a renewable alternative to fossil fuels, plays a key role in reducing greenhouse gas emissions and promoting sustainable energy solutions. However, the biodiesel production process encounters challenges particularly the evaporation of methanol after biodiesel production leads to significant environmental impacts. In addition to the environmental degradation the presence of methanol in biodiesel has adverse effects on the fuel filter for use in engines. This study summarizes the recovery of methanol from the biodiesel production process for its reuse to reduce the global warming potential over the life cycle. The study used transesterification reaction followed by the recovery of methanol in a specially designed methanol recovery chamber, its chemical analysis to ensure the quality of methanol captured an environmental impact assessment for comparison. It was recorded that with the recovery of 35% methanol will not only reduce the cost but also reduce the GHG emission by 19%. In alignment with the Punjab government policy 2018 this work contributes to cleaner biodiesel production by utilizing waste cooking oil as feedstock. Furthermore, the implementation of such recovery methods will enhance overall efficiency and lead to sustainable waste management practices to minimize the environmental impact, contributing towards net zero.

articleTitle: Precision powered: revolutionize energy consumption forecasting using transformers
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: The enormous and increasing impacts of urbanization and demographic shifts in Pakistan on energy demand are causing huge obstacles for energy management which is happening at a time when we are facing an acute energy crisis. The demand-supply gap is widening, necessitating the development of state-of-the-art models for forecasting energy consumption using machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL). Previous models like Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA) and Seasonal Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (SARIMA) helped to interpret consumption behavior insights. The major contribution of this paper is proposing and applying the new Sequential Transformer model which significantly provides an improvement over traditional models such as ANN, Vanilla Transformer, and Long short-term Memory (LSTM) giving prediction performance with better accuracy having lower computational cost. Our proposed model has a lower mean squared error (MSE), converges faster, and is more robust in predicting electricity consumption through extensive evaluations on two benchmark household electricity consumption datasets. In particular, our Sequential Transformer reaches MSE values of 0.012 and 0.115 on the two datasets, respectively, outperforming best alternative models by a large margin. This is a significant development that will help alleviate Pakistan’s energy crisis as it allows for accurate and real-time strategies for managing electricity potentially leading to timely decisions on energy generation based on consumption forecasting. Index Terms—Energy Consumption, Transformer, Deep Learning, Long short-term memory (LSTM), Predictive Modeling, Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA), Seasonal Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (SARIMA).

articleTitle: Multimodal gaze shift model using vision and auditory information for humanoid robot
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: Humanoid robots, which are made to resemble people, are essential for helping people with a variety of jobs. By creating a system that enables a humanoid robot to adjust its gaze to significant locations in its surroundings utilizing both aural and visual inputs, our goal in this work is to improve human-robot interaction. To develop a system that effectively blends acoustic and visual information, we take inspiration from disciplines such as human-computer interaction, machine learning, and neuroscience. Our method uses a neural network type of computer program to create a "map" that highlights important places depending on what the robot sees and hears. The robot's eyes follow this map to determine where to gaze. To assess how well our system performs. Through this research, our goal is to improve human-robot interaction and collaboration, resulting in more seamless and productive exchanges.

articleTitle: Double H-bridge interleaved LLC converter with wide charging range and low output voltage ripples
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: This paper proposes a double half-bridge Interleaved LLC resonant converter with wide charging range and low output voltage ripples for dc-dc stage of electrical vehicle battery charger. The proposed converter consists of two parallel half-bridge LLC converters and has dual operating mode; combined and Independent. In the prior mode, both half-bridge converters operate simultaneously but in the later mode, single converter operates. Proposed interleaved converter has the ability to achieve wide output voltage using 180° phase shift between two switches of both half-bridge converters while using 90° phase shifted gate pulses of both converters in combined mode. By adapting this technique, output voltage ripples reduce drastically. When compared to the latter option, the former method produces a gain that is twice as great. The result is a broader output volta ge range when mode change and frequency control are coupled. The results demonstrate that when operated in combined mode with straightforward frequency control, the converter produces a broad 100-420 V output voltage range. The output range extends to 50-420 V thanks to dual frequency and mode shifting control. The proposed method reduces output voltage ripples which increases the quality of charging voltage to enhance the battery life span.

articleTitle: Performance comparison of contra-rotating flux modulated machine with consequent pole configuration
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: In order to utilize the maximum efficiency of wind energy, the inner stator (IS), outer stator (OS), and inner stator consequent pole (ISCP) configurations of integrated flux modulated machine (IFMM) are compared in this paper based on the finite element analysis (FEA). To achieve more power compared to conventional machines, the IFMM consists of two rotors connected to two contra-rotating wind turbine blades, and two sets of decoupled winding exist on the stator due to which the control complexity reduces. This study analyses the electromagnetic performance comparison in terms of back-emf, flux linkage, cogging torque, Load torque, output power, and efficiency on OS-IFMM, CP-IFMM, and IS-IFMM. The results indicate that IS-IFMM machines exhibit high torque and output power, but in terms of cost, the CP-IFMM machine is a better candidate for wind power generation.

articleTitle: FEM simulation and experimental validation of a high-frequency induction heating system with COMSOL Multiphysics
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: The induction heating technique is generally used in biomedical, steel melting, and welding industries due to its higher heat ing efficiency. This technique is applied to heat-conductive materials having a nonlinear behaviour. The analytical and numerical methods are applied for modelling induction and direct resistance heating processes. The simulation design and the empirical validation of an induction heating system are presented in this paper. The simulation model of an induction heating system is developed using COMSOL Multiphysics software. The temperature distribution inside the coil, the effect of the coil’s temperature on the heating efficiency, and coil inductance is analyzed. The electrical simulation of a high-frequency power converter is performed using Multisim software. The prototype of a 1 kW induction heating system having 115 kHz frequency is developed and the measurement results are analyzed. The analysis of both simulation and experimental results are discussed.

articleTitle: LLC resonant partial power step-up DC-DC converter
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: An LLC resonant partial power converter (LLC-RPPC) for direct current step-up applications is presented. In the proposed LLC-RPPC, a major part of electrical power flows to the load at approximately 100% efficiency and only a part of electrical power is processed through LLC resonant converter. Accordingly, the proposed LLC-RPPC can be designed to attain an overall efficiency of above 90% under all operating conditions. The converter has several advantages over conventional counterparts such as lower switching losses, less EMI loss, and higher efficiency. The structure, operation, and analysis of the proposed LLC-RPPC is described in this paper. The operation and performance of the proposed LLC-RPPC is evaluated through experimental results. For this purpose, a laboratory prototype of the proposed LLC-RPPC rated at 85W was designed, built, and tested. The results obtained from experimentation are given in the paper. The results reveal excellent ZVS and ZCS switching performance of switches and diodes on the primary and secondary sides respectively over the entire range of operations.

articleTitle: Performance analysis of VLC-based Li-Fi NLOS underwater channel using ask modulation scheme over WDM under the influence of ambient light
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: Li-Fi is another term for Visible light communication (VLC) which operates by transmitting data through free space by using eith er Light Emitting Diodes (LEDs) or Laser Diodes (LDs). The technique finds substantial applications in scientific research as we ll as military applications when used underwater. VLC technology helps eliminate radio interference alongside providing replacement solutions for traditional underwater communication systems. The research develops and models a visible light wireless communication system through ambient light testing with two 550 nm and 450 nm LD light sources and Pin photodetector over 10 meters using Opti System software. The system uses Non-Return-to-Zero On-Off Keying (NRZ OOK) also known as Amplitude Shift Keying (ASK) modulation through Mach-Zehnder Modulator with WDM technology in NLOS environment. A 10 Gbps data transmission occurs through the clear ocean environment along a 10-meter channel with 0.0405 1/m absorption and 0.0025 1/m scattering. The 550 nm transmitted source emits its maximum Quality factor as 8.35 when BER analyzers operate under ambient light conditions and produce its minimum BER as 4.89e-11 under the same conditions. Examining similar ambient light influences reveals the BER analyzers demonstrate a maximum Quality factor of 8.62 and minimum BER of 18.11e-12 when operating under 450 nm transmitted light.

articleTitle: Data-driven approach for power flow direction estimation in presence of renewable energy
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: Knowledge of power flow directions in electrical grids is crucial for maintaining grid stability, efficiency, and effective resource utilization. This paper suggests a technique based on data analysis to estimate power flow directions in a power grid by utilizing Deep Neural Networks (DNNs). The DNN model is developed using an extensive dataset obtained from power flow simulations carried out on the IEEE 14-bus system, which includes real-time load profile information and solar generation data. The model leverages the system's active and reactive power injections as input to accurately forecast power flow directions across each transmission line. Notably, Gaussian noise is introduced into the dataset to enhance its robustne ss and address potential measurement errors. This method could enhance the grid monitoring and control capabilities, particularly in situations where real-time data acquisition might be compromised.

articleTitle: Adaptive sliding modes based steering protocol design for underwater vehicles with partially functional actuators
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: This paper presents a simple steering control algorithm for an underwater vehicle which is an example of nonholonomic drift free systems. The method is based on adaptive sliding mode control technique which does not require the model conversion into chain form. In the proposed steering control algorithm, some suitable Hurwitz sliding surfaces and a Lyapunov function are selected. The adaptive laws are derived while keeping Lyapunov function strictly negative to guarantee the stability of the closed loop system. The proposed method is tested on two different underwater vehicle models; in the first model all actuators are working, and in the second model one actuator is not working. The controllability Lie Algebra of the first model when all actuators are working, contains Lie brackets of depth one while the second model when one actuator fails contain Lie brackets of depth one and two. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified through simulation studies.

articleTitle: Stereo vision based navigation for driverless cars and obstacle avoidance
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: By combining autonomous driving technology with stereo vision systems, progress towards fully autonomous vehicles is becoming increasingly evident. The main goal of this project is to develop an advanced control system for a driverless car. The system is trained in this way it identifies different obstacles in the surroundings. System robustness and reliability are assessed through rigorous testing in various settings as part of an experimental setup, such as inclement weather and challenging terrain. Traffic safety is a serious issue that can be navigated through the navigation system of driverless car by reducing accidents caused by human mistakes, which is a major global contributor to traffic accidents. On the base of an algorithm, the system can detect anything and path planning. It shows how navigation systems based on stereo vision have the potential to transform the autonomous industry and increase traffic efficiency.

articleTitle: Maximizing biodiesel yield using mixture of waste cooking oil and mustard oil via RSM and ANN techniques
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: This research presents an exceptional study aimed at optimizing biodiesel production from an innovative blend of waste cooking oil (WCO) and Mustard oil (MO). Addressing the cold flow properties of WCO and the unique characteristics of MO, mixture of these two oils have been utilized and a combination of Response Surface Methodology (RSM) and Artificial Neural Network (ANN) techniques used to maximize biodiesel yield. The operating parameter, including reaction speed, RPM (100 – 500 rpm), reaction time (1-3 hours), catalyst concentration (0.2 – 2% w/w), methanol to oil ratio (8:1– 12:1 v/v), and reaction temperature (50 - 60 ℃ ). The maximum actual/experimental biodiesel yield of 95% was found at reaction speed of 500rpm, catalyst concentration of 1.1 w/w, reaction time of 2 hours, methanol to oil ratio of 10:1, and reaction temperature 55 ℃. By systematically comparing the efficiency of RSM and ANN, This extraordinary research not only advances the field of biodiesel production but also contributes significantly to addressing the pressing global challenges of energy sustainability and reduced reliance on fossil fuels. The interaction of the several operating parameters on biodiesel yield has been investigated using two methodologies: Response Surface Methodology (RSM) and Artificial Neural Network (ANN). RSM provides better modeling of parameter interaction, while ANN exhibits lower comparative error when predicting biodiesel yield based on the reaction parameters. The percentage improvement in prediction of biodiesel yield by ANN is found to be 12% as compared to RSM. For training, the R2 value is almost equal to 0.9991011, and for validation, it is 0.9540232. This study emphasizes the merits of both techniques’ response surface methodology and artificial neural network for the prediction of optimum biodiesel yield.

articleTitle: Performance of permanent magnet synchronous machines based on different winding arrangements and magnetization patterns
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: This paper investigates the performance of surface-mounted permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSMs) with two distinct winding configurations and three magnetization patterns. The winding arrangements studied include a 9-slot/10-pole PMSM with single-tooth wound coils and a 15-slot/4-pole PMSM with distributed windings. Both motor designs feature surface-mounted permanent magnets (PMs) on the rotor, with magnetization patterns configured as parallel, radial, and segmented Halbach respectively. PMSMs are widely used in applications such as electric vehicles and renewable energy systems, where high efficiency and performance are critical. This research examines the sensitivity of motor performance to winding configurations and magnetization patterns through finite element simulations in ANSYS Maxwell 2D. Key performance metrics analyzed include airgap flux density, phase back-EMF, cogging torque, and motor output torque. The findings highlight how these design variations influence motor efficiency, average torque, and torque ripple. By comparing the strengths and weaknesses of each configuration, the study identifies optimal combinations of windings and magnetization patterns for specific applications. The results offer valuable insights into PMSM design, aiding in the development of more efficient and reliable motors. This research contributes to informed decision-making in motor design and manufacturing processes, supporting the advancement of modern industrial and energy applications.

articleTitle: Design and fNIRS based control of 2-DOF exo-ankle for gait rehabilitation
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: This study presents the design and control of an ankle-assistive exoskeleton utilizing functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS). Ankle-related impairments are a major cause of mobility hindrance, often resulting in gait imbalances and abnormal walking patterns. The proposed exoskeleton is designed to provide two degrees of freedom (2-DOF), enabling active dorsiflexion and plantarflexion movements, along with passive eversion and inversion. The mechanical structure incorporates linear actuators and a ball-and-socket joint, which are controlled through brain signals. Furthermore, this study develops and implements an innovative fNIRS-based control system capable of detecting hemodynamic changes in the brain associated with ankle movements. After pre-processing the fNIRS signals, a machine learning model is trained to accurately predict the intended ankle movements. The results demonstrate that fNIRS-based control for ankle-assistive exoskeletons holds significant potential for future applications in gait rehabilitation.

articleTitle: Comparative analysis of PSC-SPWM and NLM in modular multilevel converters
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: Modular Multilevel Converter is very popular converter topology in high-power applications due to its several advantages. For MMCs, selection of a modulation technique impacts the overall efficiency of converter in terms of harmonic distortion. Therefore, understanding specific criteria of each modulation technique is crucial for optimizing MMC operation. This study compares two modulation techniques, Phase-Shifted Carrier SPWM and Nearest Level Modulation (NLM) to determine the more effective method in reducing total Harmonic Distortion in MMC converters. The comparative analysis is taken across varying submodule configurations of MMC on MATLAB/Simulink to evaluate the harmonic content generated by each method. The results provide suitability of PSC-SPWM and NLM techniques for reducing THD in MMC at varying submodule configurations which is useful for engineers and researchers in selecting the most effective modulation technique based on the specific requirement of converter.

articleTitle: Adaptive exponential reaching laws and high-gain observers for enhanced PMSM sliding mode control systems
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: This research presents a novel Adaptive Hybrid Exponential Reaching Law (AHERL) designed to enhance sliding mode control (SMC) systems for Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors (PMSMs). The method incorporates an adaptive exponential component to facilitate rapid convergence with minimal overshoot, complemented by a high-gain disturbance observer for effective disturbance compensation. The simulation results reveal that AHERL delivers exceptional performance, including a 52% decrease in the integral square error (ISE), which quantifies the cumulative squared errors over time, and a 35% reduction in the integral time-weighted absolute error (ITAE), which evaluates time-weighted control errors. Moreover, AHERL achieved the target speed regulation within 0.1014 seconds, substantially outperforming the Conventional Exponential Reaching Law (CERL) at 0.335 seconds and other approaches, thereby demonstrating superior robustness and accuracy. These results underscore AHERL’s potential to significantly enhance speed control in PMSM applications.

articleTitle: Predicting short-term traffic with random forest: a granular data approach
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: Accurate short-term traffic flow prediction is critical for improving the efficiency of Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS), particularly in heterogeneous traffic environments. This paper presents a data-driven model based on the Random Forest (RF) algorithm to predict traffic flow using high-resolution data collected over a week. The dataset encompasses individual vehicle speed, vehicle classification (car, bicycle, motorbike, bus), timestamp, flow rate, peak hour factor, traffic density, time and distance headway, and density range, recorded from 9 AM to 5 PM over seven consecutive days. Six days of data are used for training the RF model, with Thursday’s traffic flow serving as the test case. The dataset features high-dimensional, heterogeneous traffic attributes, enabling the model to capture non-linear and complex interactions effectively. Our results demonstrate that the RF model effectively captures complex, non-linear relationships in the data, delivering highly accurate predictions with an R-squared value of 0.997. This study contributes to advancing machine learning applications in traffic management, emphasizing the importance of feature selection in enhancing model performance. Future research will investigate the inclusion of additional factors such as weather conditions and external events to further refine prediction accuracy.

articleTitle: Systematic review on the design and implementation of the braille system on packaging
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: The objective of this RSL is to analyze the impact of the Braille system on packaging design to improve accessibility and autonomy for people with visual impairments. The methodology was based on four PICO questions focused on identifying the difficulties faced by these people, the technologies used, the contexts of application and the benefits to their quality of life. A PRISMA protocol was applied for the selection of studies, resulting in 28 relevant investigations. The results indicate that the Braille system, combined with advanced technologies such as IoT, NFC and 3D models, has allowed greater autonomy in the interaction with consumer products. However, technical problems were detected such as low quality in Braille prints, user mistrust and negative perceptions in some cases. Likewise, limitations are observed in the uniformity of Braille implementation and unequal access to advanced technologies, especially in regions with limited resources. It is concluded that the Braille system represents a significant advance in accessibility. However, more comprehensive, cost-effective and adaptable solutions are required to encourage mass adoption and ensure their effectiveness, especially in public environments and less technologically advanced communities.

articleTitle: Development of a convolutional neural network model for solar panel fault detection with preventive maintenance reporting options
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: As the global demand for renewable energy continually increases, operational efficiency and reliability of photovoltaic (PV) systems have become increasingly crucial. Solar panels or photovoltaic modules are susceptible to various anomalies such as cracks, electrical damage, and hotspots, which can significantly reduce their energy output if not detected early. Convention al or manual inspections are inadequate and prone to human error, especially in large-scale solar farms. This paper introduces the development of a Convolutional Neural Network Model for Solar Panel Fault Detection with a Preventive Maintenance Reporting System, which uses machine learning, thermal imaging, and cloud-based data processing to identify real-time faults. The system architecture integrates high-resolution visual cameras and thermal cameras with a Raspberry Pi4 microcontroller, the core of the system is a deep learning model based on a lightweight Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) analysis captured images to identify defects such as cracks, hotspots, and electrical damages. This data is processed in the cloud, where the anomaly detection model classifies faults with an overall accuracy of 95% with user-friendly web dashboard for monitoring and reporting, preventive maintenance measures. The results show that the CNN model significantly enhances inspection accuracy, reduces operational downtime, and lowers maintenance costs by identifying issues early.

articleTitle: FPGA-based implementation of CNN for Covid-19 identification
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: Despite advancements in treatment, the Coronavirus (Covid-19) remains a significant respiratory threat following the 2019 pandemic. Continuous efforts to enhance detection and diagnosis are crucial. Traditional methods, such as chest radiological imaging and computed tomography, are hindered by manual examination, leading to delays and potential errors. This study introduces a rapid and precise Covid-19 detection system utilizing the AlexNet Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model on the DE1 SoC FPGA platform. The methodology encompasses ten stages: acquisition of CXR image datasets, dataset segmentation, installation of the Caffe framework, LMDB dataset formatting, generation of dataset image means, CNN model training, extraction of model weights, evaluation via confusion matrices, OpenCL environment setup, and PipeCNN compilation. The anticipated outcomes include reduced operation times and enhanced accuracy.

articleTitle: AWARE-NET: adaptive weighted averaging for robust ensemble network in deepfake detection
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: Deepfake detection has become increasingly important due to the rise of synthetic media, which poses significant risks to digital identity and cyber presence for security and trust. While multiple approaches have improved detection accuracy, challenges remain in achieving consistent performance across diverse datasets and manipulation types. In response, we propose a novel two-tier ensemble framework for deepfake detection based on deep learning that hierarchically combines multiple instances of three state-of-the-art architectures: Xception, Res2Net101, and EfficientNet-B7. Our framework employs a unique approach where each architecture is instantiated three times with different initializations to enhance model diversity, followed by a learnable weighting mechanism that dynamically combines their predictions.Unlike traditional fixed-weight ensembles, our first-tier averages predictions within each architecture family to reduce model variance, while the second tier learns optimal contribution weights through backpropagation, automatically adjusting each architecture's influence based on their detection reliability.Our experiments achieved state-of-the-art intra-dataset performance with AUC scores of 99.22% (FF++) and 100.00% (CelebDF-v2), and F1 scores of 98.06% (FF++) and 99.94% (CelebDF-v2) without augmentation. With augmentation, we achieve AUC scores of 99.47% (FF++) and 100.00% (CelebDF-v2), and F1 scores of 98.43% (FF++) and 99.95% (CelebDF-v2). The framework demonstrates robust cross-dataset generalization, achieving AUC scores of 88.20% and 72.52%, and F1 scores of 93.16% and 80.62% in cross-dataset evaluations.

articleTitle: Systematic review of photovoltaic energy as an alternative energy source in business buildings
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: The objective of this SLR study is to determine the impact of photovoltaic systems as an energy alternative for commercial buildings. The study was structured using the PICO framework and data collection followed PRISMA guidelines to ensure a rigorous and reproducible methodology. In this regard, 25 articles were found that are related to photovoltaics as an alternative energy source. The results show this energy in commercial buildings reduces operating costs, dependence on fossil fuels and greenhouse gas emissions. It facilitates environmental certifications such as LEED, improves the quality of the electrical supply and allows access to energy in remote areas. Monocrystalline and bifacial panels maximize efficiency, while technological advances optimize safety and performance. It is concluded that photovoltaic energy transforms the energy management of commercial buildings, reducing costs, emissions and dependence on non-renewable sources. In addition, it improves the quality of supply, facilitates environmental certifications and promotes sustainability through advanced and efficient technology. It is suggested that further emphasis be placed on research and innovations such as monocrystalline and bifacial panels and automated cleaning technologies, in order to maximise energy efficiency, reduce operating costs and improve sustainability in commercial buildings.

articleTitle: Automated question generation from job descriptions using large language models: an evaluation of role-fit and fairness
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: This paper introduces an automated framework for generating high-quality, role-specific interview questions directly from complex job descriptions using an ensemble of Large Language Models (LLMs). We leverage seven advanced LLMs (gemma2-9b-it,gemma-7b-it,llama-3.3-70b-versatile,llama-3.1-8b-instant,llama3-70b-8192,mixtral-8x7b-32768, andOpenAI-3.5) to produce a diverse pool of questions. Our approach integrates prompt engineering and debiasing strategies to ensure that the generated questions are contextually relevant, role-aligned, and free from harmful biases. We compare the LLMs’ outputs against a strong baseline (ChatGPT o1 Pro) and human domain experts’ assessments, employing a multi-faceted evaluation framework including relevance, clarity, specificity, and fairness metrics. Our results, validated on a curated set of job descriptions across multiple industries, demonstrate that a multi-model generation strategy, combined with bias mitigation and expert-informed prompt design, yields superior interview question sets. This research offers insights into enhancing recruitment practices, improving efficiency, and fostering equitable candidate assessment.

articleTitle: Experimental assessment of an indirect evaporative heat and mass exchanger for improving the water footprints
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: Several countries, including Pakistan, are classified as water-scarce nations, with per capita water availability falling below 1,000 cubic meters. Additionally, many nations face significant water stress due to factors such as urban population growth, agricultural demands, climate change, and poor water management systems. This study examines the performance of an Indirect Evaporative Heat and Mass Exchanger for water recovery from exhaust air, utilizing a combination of hydrophobic sheet and mesh cloth. In the current system, a filter composed of these materials is employed to extract water from the working air stream. The experimental findings indicate that this configuration achieves water recovery rates of up to 60 l/h without additional power consumption. Moreover, the amount of recovered water results in ultimate values for the energy efficiency ratio and specific reduction in water footprint, ranging from 15 to 92 and 2.8 to 9.6 litres per hour per ton, respectively.
