These results demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed system, highlighting its potential for enhanced water footprints of the system with low energy requirements, thus contributing to sustainable water management solutions.

articleTitle: CowAnalyzer: visual features based smart breed identification application
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: In Pakistan, a huge portion of the agricultural Gross Domestic Product (GDP) depends on the trade of high-quality breeds which is beneficial for the livestock sector. However, more than 80% of livestock breeds in Pakistan are non-descriptive, which burdens the economy as we are unaware of their potential. Livestock breed identification is thus important for tractability, animal trading, and enhancing GDP growth. Therefore in this work, we proposed a visual features-based smart breed identification application called CowAnalyzer. The CowAnalyzer performs fast, easy-to-use, cost-effective, and reliable cow breed variates classification. It performs visual feature engineering of 10 Pakistan’s cattle breeds, by utilizing morphological, color, pattern, structure, shape, and external organ-specific features. The feature engineering is then utilized by the AI model for the identification of breeds. The CowAnalyzer achieved an overall accuracy of 79% with a moderate success rate for all breeds. The CowAnalyzer is deployed on the PakSupercomputing cluster which provides an easy-to-access and valuable platform for livestock industries including cattle farms and dairy farms.

articleTitle: Design and benchmarking of a low-cost RISC-V-based high-performance computing cluster for edge computing
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: The exponential growth of IoT devices has led to a increase in data generation, necessitating real-time processing for critical decision-making, all while ensuring energy efficiency and privacy. Edge computing addresses these challenges by reducing latency through localized processing, but many edge devices still face limitations in real-time performance, energy efficiency, and scalability. In this work, we propose an energy-efficient, low-power HPC cluster based on single-board computers and open hardware. This cluster scales HPC capabilities with low-power, open-source solutions, making it ideal for IoT applications such as predictive maintenance in smart factories and real-time patient monitoring in healthcare. Our 10-node cluster, each featuring a StarFive JH7110 64-bit Quad-core CPU with an integrated GPU, achieves significant performance improvements. The computation time for a 1000x1000 matrix is reduced from 10.39 seconds on a single node to 1.637 seconds on 10 nodes, resulting in a 63% speedup. We introduce a custom distributed logistic regression algorithm designed for RISC-V, allowing model training on a cluster with improved scalability and performance. Our results show significant speedup in training time, with up to 5.6 times faster convergence as the number of nodes increases to 10. This work demonstrates the potential of RISC-V-based systems for efficient and distributed AI model training, making them well suited for decentralized applications in fields like academia, healthcare and finance while facilitating role of RISC-V in HPC.

articleTitle: Development and performance assessment of a solar dryer in Quetta, Balochistan, Pakistan
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: This study details the design, construction, and performance analysis of a solar dryer optimized for efficient apple drying i n resource-limited environments. The dryer includes a drying chamber with a 3.5 ft² area and 5.25 ft³ volume, equipped with perforated steel trays, a solar heater, and a DC-powered air blower to ensure uniform airflow. Experiments were conducted at three airflow rates (5, 9, and 12 m/s) during peak solar conditions in July and August 2023. The system successfully reduced apple moisture content from 78% to 19% within 6 hours, achieving drying rates between 0.66–0.83 kg/h. The drying chamber-maintained temperatures 10–15°C higher than ambient, with solar irradiance ranging from 680 to 925 W/m². Fabrication costs totalled 60,000 PKR, with a projected payback period of 0.48 years based on an annual drying capacity of 2 tons. Compared to traditional sun drying, the solar dryer demonstrated greater efficiency, minimized contamination risks, and improved product quality. This scalable and energy-efficient technology provides a practical solution for food preservation in rural and underdeveloped regions, supporting sustainability goals and enhancing food security for small-scale agricultural communities.

articleTitle: Utilizing biomass for sustainable energy: a focus on power plants in Malaysia
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: Currently, fossil fuels—specifically, coal, natural gas, and occasionally oil—are the primary fuel source for power plants in Southeast Asia. In several Southeast Asian nations, including the Philippines, Vietnam, and Indonesia, coal is the most common fuel used to generate electricity. Due to its economic advantages, coal has been favored by Indonesia's domestic energy strategy, and the country is a significant producer and exporter of coal. To fulfil its increasing energy needs, Vietnam has also made significant investments in coal-fired power facilities. Southeast Asia's energy industry is one of the fastest-growing sources of greenhouse gas emissions due to the usage of fossil fuels, which puts global climate goals at risk. With major environmental and financial advantages, biomass fuel—especially agricultural waste like rice husks, wood pellets, and palm oil biomass—is becoming more widely acknowledged as a competitive alternative to fossil fuels for power generation. For instance, palm oil residues can be co-fired with coal to achieve higher boiler efficiencies while reducing net carbon emissions. Government initiatives like Malaysia’s National Biomass Strategy 2020, along with regional cooperation, are driving the adoption of biomass across Southeast Asia. Despite challenges such as supply chain issues and technological constraints, biomass holds significant potential to contribute to renewable energy targets and support sustainability goals. The aim of this paper is to examine the current state of biomass co-firing in Malaysia's power plants, focusing on the operational challenges it poses to boiler integrity and discussing practical mitigation strategies to support sustainable energy generation.

articleTitle: Advancing intrusion detection with ML and deep learning: a comparative approach
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: In network security, Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) is increasingly important due to rise in cyber-attacks. To ensure accurate detection and prevention, IDS leverages Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL) algorithms on benchmark datasets; CICIDS2017 and NSL-KDD. These datasets, with diverse attack types, are ideal for training and testing. Traditional IDS struggle to detect zero-day attacks due to lack of predefined signatures, leading to higher false positive rates and vulnerabilities. Our proposed methodology focuses on a DL-based NIDS. We pre-process and normalize data from CICIDS2017, NSL-KDD, and a custom home network dataset. Supervised ML models, including Random Forest, Decision Tree, and Gaussian Naive Bayes, were applied to CICIDS 2017, achieving high accuracy. For DL, BiLSTM and Transformer models were trained on NSL-KDD for 30–60 epochs, with accuracy rates of 87%–99%. We utilized dual approach of normalization technique using Log Transformation and enhanced the Log Transformation by adding weightage to the features and retrained the model LSTM-CNN on NSL-KDD. Additionally, an LSTM-CNN model was applied to the Home Network dataset, the accuracy result of H-N Version1 was 100%.

articleTitle: Sketch to image synthesis: harnessing deep learning techniques for realistic visual transformation
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: Crime poses a significant threat to society, with rising rates in developing countries often attributed to unidentified criminals and various social factors. Traditional black-and-white sketches used by law enforcement agencies pose challenges as witnesses struggle to definitively identify suspects. In order to enhance the accuracy of identification of criminals from face sketches, we propose a deep learning based generative model that can convert face sketches into realistic colour images. The model we have proposed consists of Component Embedding (CE), Feature Mapping (FM) and Image Synthesis (IS) modules which work together to produce realistic images through the use of sophisticated feature learning techniques. The CE module captures key facial components, while FM and IS modules work in tandem to synthesise high-quality colour images from sketches. The proposed approach is evaluated on the CelebA-HQ dataset and shows better performance in both qualitative and quantitative comparison with previous methods. The contribution of this paper can help to advance the field of sketch-to-image synthesis and provide a strong solution for the problem of criminal identification challenges.

articleTitle: Development and implementation of an autonomous vehicle prototype with ADAS
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: Road traffic accidents are a significant global issue, resulting in considerable fatalities and injuries each year. The United Nations aims to decrease such incidences by 50% by 2030. Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) provide a revolutionary solution; yet, their implementation is predominantly restricted to high-priced electric vehicles, limiting their influence to affluent markets. This study advocates for a paradigm shift by showcasing the viability of an economical autonomous vehicle prototype integrated with ADAS capabilities, created using cost-efficient and readily available technology. The prototype used a Raspberry Pi as the core computing unit, incorporating ultrasonic sensors for obstacle detection, a GPS module for navigation, and a camera for traffic signal recognition. These components, while more basic and far less costly than those in premium automobiles, effectively provide essential functions such as automated braking, GPS navigation, and adherence to traffic signals. The project employs an Agile approach, enabling iterative development and swift responsiveness to input. This research demonstrates the potential of democratising ADAS technology to provide safer, smarter automobiles to under-represented socioeconomic groups. Future developments could enhance the system’s precision by integrating advanced sensors, such as LiDAR and radar, while maintaining cost-effectiveness, fostering inclusive innovation in vehicle safety.

articleTitle: Rice analyzer: morphological and structural data engineering for deep learning-based rice classification application
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: Rice is a vital food source that is consumed worldwide. With increasing genetic varieties, mixing of rice has become a major issue in Pakistan’s export market, leading to economic losses and market distortion. The multiple varieties of rice create a challenge for efﬁcient classiﬁcation, particularly in distinguishing premium Basmati varieties. The work proposes a deep learning application for rice classiﬁcation using visual images called RiceAnalyzer. The RiceAnalyzer uses the Convolution Neural Network (CNN) based deep learning model that classiﬁes four varieties of Basmati rice: Basmati 2000, Sella 1509, Kainat 1121, and Sella Basmati 1121. The data set comprises 4561 rice grain samples collected from local rice mills. The sample images are captured using a high-resolution scanner at 600 DPI. Novel data engineering techniques are used to analyze morphological, structural, and colorimetric patterns of rice grains. The model achieved an accuracy of 95.13%, with precision rates between 0.94-0.98 for individual rice varieties. The application is deployed on the PakSupercomputing cluster, which provides remote access.

articleTitle: Optimization and efficiency improvement of hybrid floating photovoltaic and thermoelectric generation system including power converter and IoT load control system
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: As acceptance of solar power rises globally, issues including efficiency and restricted land availability create more need fo r creative floating solar solutions. Furthermore, the performance of the solar panel reduces with increasing panel temperature. As the temperature rise, the PV module's output power drops 0.5% per oC and cooling the module will enhance its performance. This work presents a method based on solar photovoltaic installation on water surfaces hybrid with thermoelectric panels. The cold side of thermoelectric panels is in contact with water, while the hot side is exposed to inte nse sunlight the works as generator due to its unique properties. Moreover, maximum PV system efficiency depends on constant monitoring of the Maximum power point (MPP). In this work the PV system will be driven to maximize electricity from solar arrays in unfavourable conditions using the maximum power point tracking algorithm (MPPTs). By 2% to 3.6% respectively, the usage of thermoelectric devices based on silicon material yields rising efficiency of PV system. Simultaneously, water floating of a solar system raised the output power up to 2% of the installed PV system and an IoT based load produced load management has also been applied in this study to properly regulate electric loads.

articleTitle: Sustainable data paradigm for smart society on ambient cloud in Pakistan
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: Researchers at Ambient Cloud started to evaluate cloud frameworks in 2010 and came up with a trusted cloud framework to build a unified knowledgebase with identity management system that we have referred to as Cloud Intellect. Standards set for cloud/cyber security and society 5.0 would form our benchmarks to keep all systems related to education, agriculture, health or infrastructure interoperable over Trusted Ambient Cloud Intellect. This community cloud infrastructure would be secure and generalized to be available for use globally in society 5.0. It would be the built on the data coming in from the societal community to perform automated services. Sustainable data governance standards would therefore be required within society 5.0 that would be residing over ambient cloud that would meet for identity management and information sharing using federated learning, blockchain or IOTA mechanisms in energy efficient secure networks within the national boundaries. Researchers have laid the foundation for SmartHealth community cloud to be embedded in Ambient Cloud to instil Intelligence. A unified standard clinical data model is built which assisted to extract medical corpora to propose cloud based smart healthcare big data analytics. Standards met are Health Level Seven Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources (HL7 FHIR) and International Classification of Diseases (ICD-10). This paper outlines three experimental case studies with estimated results for establishing trusted ambient cloud intellect using cloud infrastructure with databases and application development tools like; eucalyptus or openstack.

articleTitle: Classification of 24 skin conditions using swin transformer: leveraging DermNet & healthy skin dataset
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: Skin disease classification is a pivotal task in dermatological diagnostics, often hindered by the visual similarities betwee n conditions and diverse disease presentations. Traditional convolutional neural network (CNN) models face limitations in capturing global dependencies and multi-scale features, leading to challenges in achieving high classification accuracy. To address these issues, this study leverages the Swin Transformer, a hierarchical vision Transformer architecture, to classify 24 skin conditions, including 23 diseased skin classes from the DermNet dataset and an additional healthy skin class assembled from multiple datasets. By incorporating a healthy skin class, the model addresses a critical real-world scenario, ensuring the accurate differentiation of healthy skin from diseased conditions. Unlike prior studies that merge datasets or classify subse ts of DermNet classes, our approach focuses on comprehensive coverage of all DermNet super-classes. It adds a healthy skin category, enhancing practicality and diagnostic reliability. The Swin Transformer overcomes CNN limitations by utilizing localized self-attention mechanisms and multi-scale feature extraction, achieving an accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score of 97%. These results establish the effectiveness of Swin Transformers for real-world dermatological applications and highlight their potential as a robust framework for medical image analysis.

articleTitle: Analyzing the potential of physiological signals for emotion detection in children with autism
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental disorder that affects communication, social interaction, and behavior of an individual. Studies are being conducted to understand emotions in individuals with ASD. This research is centered on the emergence of physiological signals that are a valuable tool for emotion detection. By monitoring parameters such as heart rate, skin conductance, and oxygen saturation using non-intrusive sensors to detect and understand emotional states in real-time. Considering Ekman’s model, we took happy, sad, and fear emotions. This technology not only aids in the detection of emotional distress but also facilitates personalized strategies for supporting emotional well-being in individuals with autism. Dataset collected from different schools, rehabilitation center, and university from students, autistic individuals, and bachelor programs students. Different machine learning algorithms were trained and tested on the collected dataset. KNN showed the highest accuracy when compared to SVM and Naive Bayes. An interface was developed where the predicted emotions were shown along with the recommendations to deal with them. The study demonstrates that physiological signals such as pulse rate, GSR, and SpO2 are reliable indicators for emotion detection. By leveraging machine learning models, emotional states can be effectively identified.

articleTitle: Context aware facial expression recognition with deep learning architectures
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: Facial expression recognition (FER) plays a pivotal role in applications such as mental health diagnosis, security, marketing, human-robot interaction, healthcare, education, and gaming. However, challenges like varied facial poses, uneven lighting, and the presence of facial accessories often hinder accurate detection. Traditional methods frequently struggle with effectiv e feature extraction and classification. To address these limitations, this study proposes a robust facial expression recognition architecture based on Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) coupled with advanced preprocessing techniques. The model effectively mitigates issues such as lighting variations and class imbalances while achieving enhanced recognition accuracy. A comprehensive evaluation using k-fold cross-validation was conducted on the CK+ dataset, renowned for its high-quality labeled images of primary emotions. The proposed model achieved an accuracy of 96%, significantly outperforming established benchmarks, including VGG-19 (90%), ResNet50 (92%), and MobileNet (94%). These results underscore the efficacy of the CNN-based approach in advancing FER accuracy. Future work will focus on extending this research to real-time facial expression detection, leveraging transfer learning to adapt the model to diverse datasets, and integrating emotio n recognition with multimodal data such as speech and EEG signals to broaden its applicability across industries.

articleTitle: A study of different machine learning approaches for relation discovery task
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: Relation extraction and classification, collectively referred to as relation discovery, are fundamental tasks in the ontology construction process. In recent years, numerous studies have dedicated their efforts to devising hybrid approaches, supporting inclusive innovation in computational linguistics and ontology engineering. These approaches merge traditional methods with Machine Learning (ML) or Deep Learning (DL) techniques to tackle relation discovery tasks. This research examines the applicability and efficacy of four distinct models—Support Vector Machine (SVM), Naive Bayes (NB), k-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), and Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)—in relation extraction and classification. Two different datasets, ACL RD-TEC 2.0 and ACLRelAcS, are utilized, alongside two distinct text representation methodologies, BOW and TF-IDF-BOW. An in-depth analysis of the results, including the advantages and limitations of each model, is presented in the results and discussion sections.

articleTitle: Multi heap-based optimizer
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: This paper introduces the Multi Heap-Based Optimizer (MHBO), an enhanced version of the Heap-Based Optimizer (HBO), which is inspired by corporate rank hierarchies. While HBO employs a single heap to organize solutions and update their positions based on interactions with immediate bosses and colleagues, MHBO incorporates multiple heaps to improve exploration and convergence. Key enhancements in MHBO include a novel position-updating mechanism for the root solutions of each heap, allowing inter-heap interaction, and a heap-switching phase that facilitates solution exchange among heaps to diversify the search process. MHBO is evaluated comprehensively on 24 unimodal and 25 multimodal benchmark functions, originally used in the HBO studies. These benchmarks test its ability to navigate both simple and complex search spaces with multiple local optima. Results demonstrate that MHBO consistently outperforms HBO in terms of convergence accuracy and efficiency, highlighting its ability to exploit well and balance exploration and exploitation. The proposed framework offers a promising and adaptable solution for optimization problems, especially those with complex landscapes.

articleTitle: PakSupercomputer: an open-source, scalable, and heterogeneous supercomputing platform
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: The recent advances in large vision and language models, along with generative artificial intelligence, have led to a growing demand for compute resources such as increased processing capacity, faster memory, and larger storage. In the current scenario, supercomputing is the only domain capable of solving complex and compute-intensive algorithms for large datasets. Thus, supercomputers are considered the backbone of all fields of academia, research, innovation, and commercialization. In this work, we propose and develop a Scalable Heterogeneous Supercomputer called PakSupercomputer. The PakSupercomputer uses heterogeneous processing cores, including multiple CPUs, Tensor Processing Units (TPUs), and Field Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs). An Elastic Parallel Programming framework is deployed to provide an easy-to-use programming environment. This programming environment assists high-performance computing developers in writing applications without dealing with the complexities of heterogeneous distributed hardware architectures. The results confirm that when testing benchmarks with larger-scale, complex problems and cloud computing applications, the PakSupercomputer proves to be a low-power, Quadrillion Floating-Point Operations Per Second (FLOPS) supercomputer.

articleTitle: A comparative study of deep learning models for early diagnosis of monkeypox and chickenpox
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: Image processing enhances digital images by extracting valuable information and improving clarity through edge recognition, color modification, and filtering techniques. These methods facilitate the creation of training images that enhance the robustness and generalization of neural networks, improving diagnostic efficiency and accuracy. The similar symptoms of chickenpox and monkeypox make early clinical diagnosis difficult, necessitating rapid and precise diagnostic techniques. This study uses deep learning models to tackle the problem of correctly diagnosing chickenpox and monkeypox, facilitating early diagnosis and quick medical intervention for improving public health and epidemic management. Models such as DenseNet121, DenseNet169, DenseNet201, InceptionResNetV2, InceptionV3, MobileNet, MobileNetV2, ResNet50, ResNet101, VGG16, VGG19, and Xception have been used to classify and distinguish conditions. Advanced image processing techniques, including object detection and data normalization, improve model generalization and resilience. Among the others, MobileNet and DenseNet121 achieved highest accuracy rates which is 0.9943 and 0.9914 respectively, while MobileNet offered superior speed. The DenseNet169 model has highest precision and recall which is 0.9958 and f1-score is 0.9956 with an accuracy of 0.9857. The study also demonstrates that DL models are critical in developing robust and effective systems for detecting infectious diseases, aiding in precise and efficient healthcare solutions.

articleTitle: Optimizing renewable energy integration: a hybrid energy system approach for residential applications
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: Climate change, soaring inflation and energy shortages are driving interest in Distributed Energy Sources (DES), especially in developing countries like Pakistan, where power outages disrupt daily life. Residential communities are increasingly adopting renewable energy sources (RES) and battery storage systems (BESS) to reduce reliance on utility grid and produce cheap energy compared to grid. The authors propose a hybrid energy system (HES) combining solar PV, a diesel generator, and BESS to reduce levelised cost of energy (LCOE) and emissions while addressing energy outages for a residential building in Lahore, Pakistan. The average daily utilization of selected building is around 463 kWh/day with a peak demand of 33 kW. Different configurations are designed and their techno-economic and environmental analysis is conducted using HOMER Software. In one scenario combining PV-DG-BESS-Grid, the lowest LCOE of $0.0120 was achieved, but it resulted in higher emissions due to DG dependence. A PV-BESS-Grid configuration had a slightly higher LCOE of $0.0124 but significantly lower emissions. Sensitivity analysis also revealed that PV-BESS-Grid system to be most robust among all the designed systems.

articleTitle: Enhancing electric vehicle battery performance through Grey Wolf Optimization and Deep Reinforcement Learning integration
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach for optimizing the charging-discharging schedules of electric vehicle batteries by integrating Grey Wolf Optimization (GWO) with Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL). This hybrid method leverages GWO's global search capability alongside DRL's ability to learn optimal policies on the fly, leading to enhanced battery management. Based on a dynamic battery model with standard State of Charge (SOC) representation and constraints, the optimization process prioritizes maximizing charge duration while maintaining vigilant energy usage. The results demonstrate that the proposed GWO-DRL framework achieves a 25% improvement in charging efficiency and reduces discharge energy loss by up to 30% compared to traditional methods. These results suggest the potential for significant increases in battery lifespan and dri ving range in electric vehicles while also increasing the efficiency of its operations.

articleTitle: A real-time harmonic estimation using a hybrid least square-virus colony search algorithm
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: High renewable energy penetration and trends in using power electronic devices have raised serious concerns about power quality. The non-linear nature of power electronics devices and different types of loads are the roots of producing harmonics in electrical power systems. The existence of harmonics in electrical power systems raises several concerns for users and utility. Therefore, harmonics mitigation is necessary for safe operation on both the utility and consumer side. Before harmonic mitigation, harmonic estimation is necessary to be done. This paper proposes a hybrid Least square virus colony (LS-VCS) algorithm for harmonics estimation. The proposed methodology is tested on different test signals from literature and three real-time examples including light emitting diode (LED) lamp signal, an uninterrupted power supply (UPS) signal, an axial flux permanent magnet generator (AFPMG) signal for harmonic estimation, and specifically find out the percentage of harmonic content present in their signals using an open source Mealpy python library. The proposed methodology shows improved results in harmonic estimation for different test signals and real-time signals even in the presence of inter and sub-harmonics. The proposed methodology also works well in the presence of noise.

articleTitle: Undecimated discrete wavelets transform-based image fusion and de-noising in FPGA
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: Image processing is a vast field of study and has gained significant importance in recent years. Image fusion and denoising a re most important methods in the field of image processing. The project develops an image processing system on a Field-Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) platform that uses the Undecimated Discrete Wavelet Transform (UDWT) for image fusion and denoising. By merging several images into a single better image and using sophisticated wavelet techniques to reduce noise the aim is to improve image quality. UDWT preserves image details by maintaining high-frequency components without down sampling. Reconstructing denoised images thresholding to remove noise and dividing images into wavelet coefficients are the steps in the process that culminate in the creation of a superior composite image. Due to its ability to process data in parallel the FPGA platform is preferred over conventional CPU-based techniques for processing large amounts of data quickly. Suitable for real-time applications, this method takes advantage of the intrinsic parallelism of FPGA to process data quickly and efficiently. According to the results the FPGA-based system performs faster and produces better images than traditional techniques making it a reliable option for high-performance image processing application.

articleTitle: Intelligent data-driven methods for enhancing distributed excitation control in electrical grid
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: This paper proposes a decentralized excitation control method based on synchronized estimation using asynchronous measurements from voltage/current transformers (VT/CT), addressing the challenges of decentralized excitation control caused by asynchronous updates. Due to the high cost and limited use of Phasor Measurement Units (PMUs), synchronized generator output measurements are often not feasible. The proposed method establishes a framework for decentralized excitation control that aligns with synchronized estimation in multi-machine power systems. It develops an estimation model for synchronized acquisition of excitation control feedback inputs, even under asynchronous sampling conditions. Simulation results using IEEE standard test systems demonstrate that synchronized estimated values offer a more accurate representation of the system’s status compared to asynchronous measurements, with better compatibility with the network structure. The findings show that decentralized excitation control based on synchronized estimation significantly enhances power system stability compared to traditional control methods that rely on asynchronous feedback.

articleTitle: Benchmarking YOLO-based models for palm oil tree detection: an in-depth analysis from YOLOv5X to YOLOv11X
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: This study evaluates the performance of different YOLO (You Only Look Once) models in detecting palm oil trees, a critical task for sustainable plantation management. Among the tested models, YOLOv5x demonstrated the best balance between speed and accuracy, achieving an F1-score of 93.8% and a detection time of 34 seconds, making it well-suited for real-time applications in large-scale plantations. In comparison, YOLOv10x, with a slightly higher accuracy (F1-score of 95.5% and mAP50 of 98.7%), was found less practical for time-sensitive scenarios due to its slower detection speed. The study highlights the potential of YOLOv5x to streamline plantation management tasks, such as yield estimation, health monitoring, and tree counting, significantly reducing reliance on manual labor and enabling timely responses to pest and disease outbreaks. Additionally, the versatility of YOLOv5x extends beyond palm oil plantations to broader forestry applications, including growth detection, carbon stock assessment, and ecosystem monitoring. By providing robust, efficient, and scalable solutions, this study underscores the role of advanced AI-driven detection models in promoting sustainable practices in forestry and agriculture, addressing critical challenges in resource management and environmental conservation.

articleTitle: FPGA-enabled hand gesture recognition for smart home applications
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: Machine learning (ML) algorithms trained with hand gesture data have achieved accuracy rates close to 95%. However, despite this high accuracy, a trained ML algorithm requires hardware implementation to be effectively utilized in practical applications. In the proposed approach, we select one of the three investigated ML algorithms (CNN, ResNet50, and MobileNetV2) that demonstrates the best accuracy and make it compatible with loading onto a Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA). This allows the algorithm to be effectively utilized in real-world applications. The optimized algorithm was implemented on a Zynq 7000 board to enhance performance, achieving greater efficiency, accuracy, and lower power consumption compared to traditional CPU-based or other architectures. The implementation was tested using a custom dataset containing six distinct hand gestures for detection and computation. Resource-efficient utilization led to a 2% increase in accuracy and a 5% reduction in processing time for the CNN-trained model on the FPGA compared to the CPU. Similarly, the ResNet50-trained model on the FPGA achieved 7% higher accuracy and 9% faster processing time compared to its execution on a CPU. Hand gesture recognition integrated with FPGAs can achieve real-time responsiveness, energy efficiency, and reliability, making them ideal for resource-constrained environments that demand high performance. This demonstrates the FPGA's advantage in smart home solutions, which combine accuracy, speed, and low power consumption.

articleTitle: Improved arithmetic optimization algorithm
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: The Arithmetic Optimization Algorithm (AOA) is a well-established metaheuristic optimization technique inspired by fundamental mathematical operations such as addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division. Although AOA has demonstrated strong performance in solving a variety of optimization problems, it encounters significant challenges in complex search spaces. These challenges include limited exploration capability, premature convergence to local optima, an imbalance between exploration and exploitation, and slow convergence speed. To address these challenges, this study introduces the Improved Arithmetic Optimization Algorithm (IAOA), which incorporates Random Opposition-Based Learning (ROBL) to enhance the performance of AOA. ROBL improves AOA by introducing opposite solutions, thereby diversifying the search process to enhance exploration. It also refines exploitation by ensuring a more focused search within promising regions, achieving a better balance between exploration and exploitation. These enhancements allow IAOA to navigate complex search spaces effectively, avoid local optima, and accelerate convergence toward the global solution. The performance of IAOA is evaluated on a standard set of 23 benchmark functions, including unimodal functions to test exploitation capabilities and multimodal functions to evaluate exploration. Results demonstrate that IAOA outperforms the original AOA on th e majority of benchmark functions, showcasing significant improvements in convergence speed, robustness, and overall optimization performance.

articleTitle: Systematic review on perimeter security in the detection of centralization vulnerabilities in SDN networks
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: The purpose of this systematic review is to evaluate the impact of perimeter security on the detection of vulnerabilities in SDN networks. Using the PICO tool to formulate the questions that guide this qualitative work. The study explored the security strategies implemented, comparing protected and unsecured networks. The PRISMA protocol guided the rigorous selection of relevant and high-quality articles, obtaining 50 articles directly related to perimeter security and vulnerabilities in SDN networks. The results revealed that strategies such as network segmentation, advanced firewalls, access control, and real-time monitoring significantly improve control plane protection in SDN networks. The implementation of IDS/IDPS systems optimized the detection and response to threats, increasing the resilience of the network. It is concluded that perimeter security is essential to mitigate vulnerabilities in SDN networks. However, areas of opportunity were identified to delve deeper into the distribution of control and challenges in dynamic environments. It is suggested that research be carried out on the integration of emerging technologies with SDN networks to optimize the detection of cyber threats.

articleTitle: A retrospective on the progress of renewable energy in Pakistan: trends, challenges and sustainable solutions
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: This research explores Pakistan’s potential for renewable energy, focusing on legislative and regulatory frameworks, technological advancements, investment prospects, challenges and future outlook. Pakistan is making significant progress towards clean energy solutions, thanks to the government's commitment to sustainable energy, abundant renewable resources and increased private sector engagement. This article provides a retrospective on the development of renewable energy in Pakistan by looking into the trends, challenges, and potential solutions. There are significant developments in the renewable energy infrastructure but major bottlenecks like grid access, regulatory challenges, and financial difficulties persist. This paper also analyzes the growing share of solar, wind and hydro in the energy mix and discusses how AI and other technologies can enhance future energy generation and distribution efficiencies. Strategies for correction of grid deficiencies, strengthening of regulatory regimes and boosting of private sector participation are presented. The results point towards the importance of specific changes in policies to ensure a more robust and sustainable energy future.

articleTitle: Optimized solar powered hydrogen production, storage and utilization for fuel cell electric vehicle (FCEV) model: a sustainable energy solution
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: Continue depletion of fossil fuels at an alarming rate and environmental concerns are escalate, hydrogen emerges as a green and sustainable energy source. Hydrogen has a crucial role in the transition away from fossil fuel dependent energy systems. There are multiple sources and technologies available for the production of hydrogen. A multitude of conventional methods has a significant impact on greenhouse gas emissions due to their high production costs and inefficiency. The study presents a comprehensive model for the production, storage, and utilization of green hydrogen, by addressing the inadequacies and higher costs related to conventional methods. This model incorporates a PV array to generate electricity, powering an electrolyzer that splits water into hydrogen and oxygen. The hydrogen produced is stored and then employed in a fuel cell electric vehicle that is equipped with a Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cell, thus generating electric power and powering the vehicle. The proposed system is modelled and simulated in TRNSYS software and ensures efficient and sustainable energy use for transportation by optimizing hydrogen production with solar power availability. The results show that PV system generates peak electric power from April to June, with corresponding fuel cell output peaking in August and hydrogen storage reaching 658 Nm³ in May. This allows the system to charge a Toyota Mirai car up to 12 times, providing a driving range of approximately 3552 miles during peak production months.

articleTitle: Strategic management of forecast uncertainties to mitigate power imbalances in virtual power plants
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: A Virtual Power Plant (VPP) model for optimising participation in single energy markets among different groups of power plants. An integrated architecture and nodal-based aggregation approach for analysis of a set of generation, load and storage unit models are presented in this research paper. The interactions with market participants and the associated communication patterns for day-ahead and intraday markets are defined. The forecast uncertainties of renewable energy generation are dealt with by an imbalance compensation algorithm and introduced to a three-stage multi-period optimization process. Operational constraints are properly handled through optimization problem formulation as a constrained mixed integer linear programming (MILP) problem. The model is validated through simulation studies to show how it can reduce power dynamics and improve operational effectiveness. Results indicate that control and the optimization of online bidding are essential to increase the dependability and cost efficiency of the VPP.

articleTitle: The effectiveness of performance through dead time compensation in three-level neutral-point-clamped inverter
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: A voltage-source inverter (VSI) has become an integral one of variable frequency drives in uninterruptible power supplies and modern motor controls. Power supply systems (UPS), active power filters (APF), etc. Indeed, existing technologies in power semiconductor devices, pulse width modulation, and application control have allowed the enhanced creation of powerful power conditioning devices. Even so, we still have a problem when one leg of the inverter is changed. There is generally a considerable amount of time required for the switch to shut off completely. As a result, our input source will become short - circuited if we do not take care of it. When pulse width modulation (PWM)-based inverters are used, this delay is generally referred to as dead time. It is possible to prevent bridge through by providing dead time. However, it can also result in negative consequences. Our objective in this paper is to minimize the impact of dead time by presenting a simple real-time method and its implementation compensation method, neutral point clamped (NPC) inverters, especially for three levels. The proposed method is implemented using MATLAB (Simulink). Simulations have been performed to verify the validity of the introduced three-level NPC inverter.

articleTitle: Accurate melanoma subtype classification via deep learning and dermoscopic images
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: Acral lentiginous melanomas Skin cancers such as melanoma are particularly dangerous. The likelihood of melanoma being totally cured increases with time from diagnosis. The importance of patient and clinician understanding of early melanoma symptoms cannot be overstated. Dermatologists can diagnose it with dermoscopic images. Comparison of precision, recall, f - measure, and accuracy between Stages 1 and 2 of melanoma and benign nevi because of the small differences between the two. Skin cancer studies tend to focus on determining if a lesion is melanoma or non-melanoma. Moreover, only a small amount of research has been done on the classification of subtypes of melanoma. In this study, deep learning and dermoscopic imaging were employed to identify melanoma subtypes like AM. In this research, we presented a new deep-learning model for organizing skin cancer. We categorized skin lesions from the "Yonsei University Healthcare System in South Korea" using a dermoscopic image collection. A robust automatic system for detecting acral melanoma was built through data augmentation. The evaluation of our model's performance was based on transfer learning. This study employs three pre-trained models: VGG16, the Inception V3 network, and Dense Net, which are then assembled via stacking. By using stacking, VGG 16 achieved an accuracy of 91.7241, Inception 3 achieved an accuracy of 93.1, Dense Net achieved an accuracy of 94.48, and Ensemble these models by using stacking achieved an accuracy of 97.2%.

articleTitle: Sustainable construction materials to improve environmental impact: a systematic review
publicationTitle: International Conference on Energy, Power, Environment, Control and Computing (ICEPECC 2025)
abstract: This Systematic Literature Review (SLR) analyzes the use of sustainable construction materials to improve environmental impact, focusing on their effectiveness, applications, and contributions to construction projects. The methodology combines the PICO and PRISMA frameworks: PICO guided the formulation of four research questions to identify relevant studies, while PRISMA ensured a rigorous inclusion-exclusion process, resulting in 38 key articles. Sustainable materials are essential for reducing emissions, managing waste efficiently, and optimizing construction processes through technologies like BIM and VDC. Despite global standards like LEED and BREEAM promoting their adoption, significant challenges remain in adapting these materials to resource-limited contexts. Further research is required to assess their long-term environmental and economic viability, including detailed cost comparisons with conventional materials across diverse projects. The findings demonstrate that sustainable construction materials effectively mitigate environmental impacts, enhance energy efficiency, and support innovative construction practices. However, unresolved issues, such as local adaptation and comprehensive long-term evaluations, persist. To maximize their potential, it is essential to foster innovation, strengthen regulatory frameworks, and improve accessibility to these materials. These measures will ensure wider adoption, maximize environmental benefits, and support their application in diverse regional and economic contexts.
